truth.problem: OpenRouter's balance endpoint used a doubled `/api` path (`balancePath: "/api/v1/credits"` against a `baseUrl` that already ends in `/api`) and parsed a response shape neither `/v1/credits` nor any other OpenRouter endpoint returns (`body.credits.{total,used,remaining}`).
truth.impact: `keryx providers status`, `/connect` and the routing picker's balance column always showed OpenRouter as having no balance (a 404 or a malformed body makes `fetchProviderBalance` return `undefined`), even for a correctly connected, funded key — the AC5 balance feature silently did not work for the most common hosted provider.

truth.problem: The full-refresh cache writer (`saveProviderCatalogCache`) and the single-provider patch writer `providers test` uses (`updateProviderCatalogEntry`) both wrote `provider-catalog.json` with no lock between them. A `providers test` patch landing while a slower full refresh (up to `CATALOG_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` per provider, run in parallel at `keryx shell` startup) was still in flight was silently clobbered once the older refresh finally finished and overwrote the whole file unconditionally.
truth.impact: A provider an operator had just re-tested and fixed via `providers test` (or the `/connect` row's `[Test]` button) could have that corrected entry silently reverted to an older, still-in-flight startup refresh's result — a lost update with no error and nothing on the record showing it happened.

candidate.problem: The shell startup refresh is fed `opts.detected`, but `resolveTuiStartup` (src/commands/shell.ts:2905-2930) returns `detected: []` whenever a provider+model comes from flags or from the saved config — i.e. for every returning user. `loadOrRefreshProviderCatalogFromDetected([], …)` then builds `{fetchedAt: now, providers: {}}` and `saveProviderCatalogCache` writes it (its merge only iterates the refresh's own providers, so every on-disk entry is dropped). Confirmed by running it: after an empty-detected refresh, `loadOrRefreshProviderCatalog` with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set returns no providers and makes zero fetches.
candidate.impact: On a normal `keryx shell` start with a stale/missing cache, the catalog is wiped and stamped fresh for 5 minutes. In that window `/routing`'s picker offers no providers, `/routing` and `keryx routing list` report every assignment as not connected / falling back, `keryx providers status` prints 'none — no provider is connected', and the AC6 startup failure notice can never fire. The feature's main path produces the opposite of what it claims, and the only test of this wiring is a source-text audit that cannot see it.

candidate.problem: `updateProviderCatalogEntry` overwrites the catalog-level `fetchedAt` with the single patched entry's timestamp. `isCatalogFresh` reads only that top-level field, so one `keryx providers test <name>` makes the whole catalog look fresh although no other provider was probed (or even present). Confirmed by running it: empty cache, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set, `providers test groq` -> the next `loadOrRefreshProviderCatalog` returns only groq and does not refresh.
candidate.impact: After any `providers test`, `providers status`, `/routing`'s picker and `keryx routing list` serve a partial or days-old catalog for 5 minutes: other connected providers are missing or shown with stale status/models/balance, and routing assignments to them are reported as not connected. `providers.status.test.ts` ('also updates the SAME catalog cache') asserts this behaviour instead of catching it.

candidate.problem: The 'connected' gate is skipped for every registry provider with `requiresApiKey: false`: built-in `rapid-mlx` (darwin) and all custom `llm-providers.json` entries (`customCompatProviders` forces `requiresApiKey: false`). candidate.impact: Every macOS user who does not run Rapid-MLX gets 127.0.0.1:8010 probed on each refresh, sees 'Rapid-MLX (Local): unreachable' in `providers status`, and (once G1 is fixed, or on first-run startup where detected is populated) a 'Rapid-MLX (Local): unreachable — /connect to fix' startup notice on every launch. Contradicts the documented 'An unconnected provider is never probed and never listed'. The tests avoid it by pinning `platform: "linux"`.
